evidence.description: Core ADC read function. Accesses ADC_CON (0xB800E000) to select channel via bits [11:9], starts conversion (bit 0x2000), polls completion (bit 0x40000), reads 10-bit result from ADC_XDATA (+0xC). Used by voltage monitoring functions.
Reads battery voltage from ADC channel 2. Applies 3-stage scaling. About screen shows ~9.09V.
Reads V3V3 voltage from ADC channel 3. About screen displays ~7.97V despite name suggesting 3.3V rail - likely voltage divider or different rail.

VSYS voltage - returns float constant 5.0f (0x40A00000 @ 0x2debc). INCONSISTENCY: About screen displays 6.00V. No ADC read performed - value may be updated elsewhere or scaling happens in UI renderer.
Touch screen ADC initialization. Configures Wait-for-Trigger mode (ADC_CON bits [15:14]=11). Enables APB clock, sets conversion delay, disables MAV filter. Hardware triggers interrupt on stylus-down.
Touch data consumer - does NOT access ADC registers directly. Reads from RAM buffers populated by interrupt handler. Dominated by memcpy operations and UI calls.
N32903 ADC chapter 6.24. Defines register map, touch modes (normal/semi-auto/auto/wait-for-trigger), 4-wire resistive touch with embedded switches. ADC_BA = 0xB800E000.
Hardware: Touch screen connected to pins 57-60 (ADC_TP_YM/XM/XP/YP). 4-wire resistive type with switches integrated in SoC - no external GPIO muxing required.

raw_note:
**ADC Register Map (N32903 SoC):**

Base: 0xB800E000 (pointers at 0x2dfdc and 0x8b034)

- ADC_CON (0xB800E000): Control register
  - [17] ADC_EN: Enable ADC block
  - [15:14] ADC_TSC_MODE: 00=Normal, 01=Semi-Auto, 10=Auto, 11=Wait-for-Trigger
  - [13] ADC_CONV: Start conversion (auto-clears)
  - [11:9] ADC_MUX: Channel select (0-1=unused, 2=VADJ, 3=VIN, 4=N/A, 5-6=touch)
  - [0] ADC_FINISH: Conversion status

- ADC_TSC (0xB800E004): Touch screen control
  - [9] ADC_TSC_MAV_EN: Moving average filter enable
  - [8] ADC_TSC_XY: X(0) or Y(1) position select (semi-auto)
  - [7:4] XP/XM/YP/YM: Manual switch control (normal mode only)
  - [2:1] ADC_TSC_TYPE: 00=4-wire, 01=5-wire, 10=8-wire
  - [0] ADC_UD: Stylus up/down state (read-only)

- ADC_DLY (0xB800E008): Conversion delay
- ADC_XDATA (0xB800E00C): X-position / normal ADC data (10-bit)
- ADC_YDATA (0xB800E010): Y-position data (10-bit)
- TSC_MAV_X (0xB800E098): MAV filtered X-data
- TSC_MAV_Y (0xB800E09C): MAV filtered Y-data

**Complete ADC Channel Assignment:**

Channel 0 (AIN0, Pin 62): UNUSED - no firmware access
Channel 1 (AIN1, Pin 63): UNUSED - no firmware access
Channel 2 (AIN2, Pin 64): VADJ - Nozzle/Printhead voltage → ~9.09V displayed
Channel 3 (AIN3, Pin 66): VIN - Input voltage → ~7.97V displayed
Channel 4: Does not exist (only 4 analog inputs AIN0-3)
Channel 5-6: Touch Panel (dedicated TP pins, not normal AINs)

V5V0: Software constant 5.00f (0x40A00000 @ 0x2debc) - USB/Boost rail, NOT an ADC channel

**Voltage Monitoring Functions:**

adc_read_channel (0x2df28): Core ADC function, channels 2-3 only
voltage_read_vadj (0x2dee8): Reads channel 2, 3-stage scaling → 9.09V (nozzle)
voltage_read_vin (0x2dec0): Reads channel 3, 2-stage scaling → 7.97V (input)
voltage_read_vsys (0x2deb4): Returns constant 5.0f (no ADC read)
voltage_monitor_task (0xb3f3c): Monitors channel 3 (VIN) continuously

**Touch Screen Architecture:**

1. Hardware: 4-wire resistive touch (pins 57-60)
   - ADC_TP_XP/XM/YP/YM connected to SoC
   - Switches embedded in chip (no GPIO mux needed)

2. Initialization (adc_touch_init @ 0x8adcc):
   - Enables APB clock gate (0xB0000018)
   - Sets Wait-for-Trigger mode (ADC_CON [15:14]=11)
   - Configures conversion delay
   - Disables MAV filter

3. Operation (interrupt-driven):
   - Hardware waits for stylus-down event
   - Triggers ADC interrupt (WT_INT @ ADC_CON[20])
   - Interrupt handler reads XDATA/YDATA (NOT YET IDENTIFIED)
   - Handler stores to RAM buffers
   - touch_adc_read (0x618dc) consumes buffered data

**CRITICAL CORRECTIONS:**

1. Previous analysis incorrectly used ADC base 0xB8006000 (old/different SoC)
   Correct base: 0xB800E000 (verified from N32903 datasheet + binary)

2. Voltage function naming corrected:
   - voltage_read_vbat → voltage_read_vadj (nozzle/printhead voltage)
   - voltage_read_v3v3 → voltage_read_vin (input voltage)

3. AIN0/AIN1 are NOT audio in this device - they are simply unused

**About Screen Display (from screenshot):**
- VADJ: 9.09V (nozzle voltage)
- VIN: 7.97V (input voltage)  
- V5V0: 5.00V (constant, not measured)

**Open Questions:**

1. ADC interrupt handler location - where does it read XDATA/YDATA?
2. RAM buffer addresses for touch data
3. Exact voltage divider ratios for VADJ/VIN channels
4. Why are AIN0/AIN1 pins present but unused? Design reserve?
summary: The N32903 SoC has a 10-bit ADC at base 0xB800E000 with voltage monitoring on channels 2-3 (VADJ nozzle voltage ~9.09V, VIN input voltage ~7.97V) and resistive touch screen controller using Wait-for-Trigger mode. Channels 0-1 (AIN0/AIN1) are unused. V5V0 is a software constant (5.00V), not an ADC channel.
title: ADC Architecture: Voltage Monitoring & Touch Screen Controller
